query: What drives praise and complaints in Amazon reviews?

per_column.name: praise_signal_count
per_column.rationale: A count of praise signals is a genuine axis for driving the praise/complaint query. However groundedness is imperfect: AMZ-0004 is effusively positive ('can't get enough of it') yet scores 0, and AMZ-0005 with multiple praises scores only 1, suggesting inconsistent extraction.

per_column.name: complaint_signal_count
per_column.rationale: Directly relevant to the complaint side of the query. Sampled values are mostly defensible (disappointment=1, mixed review=1), though AMZ-0004 which explicitly has a 'negative comment' scores 0, a mild miss.

per_column.name: dominant_driver
per_column.rationale: A useful categorical for grouping reviews by praise vs complaint orientation, but it is largely a restatement of the two count columns. The strongly positive AMZ-0004 is labeled 'neutral', which contradicts its clearly praising text.

per_column.name: mentioned_aspects
per_column.rationale: Aspect tagging is the single most valuable column for identifying WHAT drives praise/complaints. However 'general' dominates 70% of rows, and AMZ-0005 tagged 'value' where the text mainly praises the film/package; extraction seems shallow but not fabricated.

per_column.name: review_length_bucket
per_column.rationale: A bucketed text-length proxy adds little analytical leverage for identifying drivers of praise/complaints; it is a generic surface feature. Values are trivially derivable from the text and correct.

per_column.name: exclamation_count
per_column.rationale: Exclamation count is a weak intensity proxy, only loosely tied to drivers of sentiment. Values are directly countable from source and sampled ones look correct.

per_column.name: has_comparison
per_column.rationale: A comparison flag can surface competitor/alternative framing that drives judgments, a reasonable axis. Sampled values plausible; near-constant (94% zero) limits leverage somewhat.

per_column.name: repeat_purchase_signal
per_column.rationale: Repeat-purchase/loyalty signal is a meaningful driver of praise. But AMZ-0004 ('using this product for many years', gave it to friends) is a clear repeat/loyalty case scored 0, showing the extractor misses obvious positives; column is also near-constant.

judge.rationale: Most columns give genuine analytical axes for the praise/complaint query: signal counts, dominant_driver, aspects, comparison and repeat-purchase flags all support grouping and modeling drivers. review_length_bucket and exclamation_count are generic surface proxies that add little leverage. Groundedness is generally acceptable but undermined by inconsistent extraction: the strongly positive AMZ-0004 is scored 0 praise, 0 complaint, 'neutral', and 0 repeat-purchase despite explicit loyalty language, and its 'negative comment' is missed — indicating the signal detectors under-fire, producing some values contradicted by the source.
